To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we can control the two- and three- photon absorption of molecules with shaped pulses.
the amplitude of the two- and three-harmonic generation signals of large organic molecules is modulated by a factor of 100 by modulating the pulse phase.
we have shown orders of magnitude control of multiphoton processes by modulating the shape of ultrafast laser light pulses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for controlling the nonlinear optical properties of large molecules in solution with femtosecond pulses.
developing a new generation of laser pulses with controlled amplitude and phase.
the control of nonlinear optical processes by modulating the temporal phase of ultrafast light pulses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed control over multiphoton processes is due to interference of the electric field in the time-domain, and not due to simple intensity changes.
multiphoton intracavity interference is a very powerful tool for the control and optimization of nonlinear optical processes.
the observed control over nonlinear excitation processes is due to the modulation of the phase of the electric field, and that this modulation is the result of a specific phase function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that multiphoton intraspulse interference is the key to controlling multiphoton processes.
we are able to modulate the amplitude and phase of the electric field of the pulse in order to modulate the nonlinear optical response.
we can use a single laser pulse to selectively excite a molecule to a higher vibrational level or to an electronically excited state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multiphoton processes can be controlled by modulating laser pulses in the temporal domain.
phase modulation of femtosecond pulses can be used to control nonlinear optical processes.
phase modulation can be used to control the amplitude of higher order nonlinear optical effects, and that this control does not rely solely on peak intensity.
